groups.label: Dialogue: Smell and Necessity
groups.summary: Socrates cites the sensation of smell as a pure pleasure experienced without antecedent suffering, and later presents the cosmic vision of the spindle of Necessity guided by the sirens and the Fates.
groups.rationale: These are the only direct dialogue passages from Books IX and X in this neighbourhood, contrasting with the remainder of the set which consists of late-volume editorial commentary and index apparatus.

groups.label: Aesthetics, Poetry, and Music
groups.summary: Editorial essays and index references examine Plato's critique of mimetic art and Homeric poetry, the moral need for censorship, and the role of musical training in shaping character.
groups.rationale: These entries all focus on Plato's treatment of aesthetic education, the criticism of poets and imitative art, and the regulatory function of music.

groups.label: Guardians and Philosopher-Kings
groups.summary: These apparatus and index entries outline the nature, strict qualifications, educational tiers, and ruling responsibilities of the guardians and philosopher-rulers.
groups.rationale: The items concentrate specifically on the ruling class of the ideal republic, detailing guardian character, their multi-stage philosophical curriculum, and governance duties.

groups.label: Polity Design and Evolution
groups.summary: Editorial notes and index citations analyze the constitutional structures of the Republic, including the descent of regimes, communal property, Spartan and Athenian origins, and distinctive institutional innovations.
groups.rationale: This group unites comprehensive editorial and index analyses addressing macro-level state design, historical influences, communal institutions, and constitutional forms.

groups.label: Apparatus: Virtues and Editorial
groups.summary: This group covers the index cataloguing of virtue across the soul and state, alongside the transcriber's closing technical notes on typographical corrections and notation.
groups.rationale: Both entries represent concluding structural elements of the reference apparatus at the absolute end of the work's paratext.
